summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with dyspnea, orthopnea, nausea, abdominal pain, and a 4kg weight gain, concerning for fluid overload and possible peritonitis. She has a complex history including type 1 diabetes, ESRD on peritoneal dialysis, gastroparesis, and is awaiting a kidney-pancreas transplant. Admission labs revealed hyponatremia, uremia, and an elevated peritoneal fluid white blood cell count with 57% neutrophils, confirming peritonitis. Cultures remained negative. She was treated with intraperitoneal vancomycin and ceftazidime, with rapid improvement in cell counts. Her volume status improved with dialysis, and her respiratory symptoms resolved. Orthostatic hypotension was noted, attributed to fluid shifts and poor oral intake due to daytime abdominal fullness. Furosemide was discontinued due to low blood pressure. Diarrhea was evaluated and found to be C. diff negative. She was transitioned to a new outpatient PD center, will complete antibiotics as an outpatient, and resume nighttime dialysis to improve nutrition and reduce symptoms. She was discharged home in stable condition.
